title: 3CX tells self-managed customers to update to V20 Update 10 for two NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities
date_note: 3CX's advisory is dated 20 November 2026; the page gives no earlier day (the NGINX flaws were published 18 November, per the same page).
summary: 3CX's advisory says two NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) affect self-managed 3CX systems; the fix is V20 Update 10, Build 20.0.10.1801. 3CX says hosted and SMB systems were already updated. Greenbone says Rapid7 published a working proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 and reports no attacks; 3CX's advisory does not mention exploitation.
plain: 3CX says its phone-system software contains two flaws from the NGINX web server. Customers who run 3CX on their own servers are told to install the newer build. Greenbone says a working proof of concept exists for one flaw.
exec: Self-managed 3CX phone systems need the vendor's update; hosted and SMB systems were already updated, according to 3CX.
action: 3CX advises self-managed customers to install V20 Update 10, Build 20.0.10.1801, and until then to restrict access to the 3CX web port (HTTPS) to the office, VPN or known IP addresses.

evidence.quote: Rapid7 published a working proof of concept
Führen Sie so bald wie möglich ein Update auf V20 Update 10, Build 20.0.10.1801 oder höher durch.

validation.note: Primary source: 3CX (3cx.de) own advisory; Borns IT Blog (borncity.com) also states the fix. Neither page mentions exploitation.
